Recovery from groundwater drought

Source: R/ind-catalog.R
lap_ind_drought_recovery.Rd

On a standardised index (see lap_ind_drought()): for each drought event (run of value < threshold), the number of timesteps from the event's minimum forward to the first value >= 0.

Usage

lap_ind_drought_recovery(
  data,
  value = gwl_norm,
  date = "date",
  threshold = -1,
  check = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A one-series data frame.

value

<tidy-select> level column.

date

<tidy-select> optional date column (used only to order the series).

threshold

Drought threshold on the index. Default -1.

check

Verify that value really looks like a standardised index. Set FALSE when you have already established that elsewhere - notably for a window of a longer standardised record, where the index legitimately sits far from zero (a well in drought for the whole window) and the check would otherwise reject exactly the driest series.

...

Ignored (uniform indicator signature).

Value

A one-row tibble with the two columns above.

Details

ind_drought_recovery_weeks

mean recovery time over events that do recover

ind_drought_n_unrecovered

number of events whose recovery is not completed within the slice

References

Peterson, T.J. et al. (2021) Nature 591, 597 (groundwater drought that may not recover). USGS groundwater-drought metrics.

See also
